analysis.investment_thesis: Bata India is a good business priced as if it were a great one: a P/E of 50.70 and P/B of 6.39 produce a Graham Number of approximately INR 262, meaning the market price of INR 757 is nearly three times the calculated intrinsic value. With a nine-year revenue CAGR of just 4.1% — barely keeping pace with inflation — there is no earnings momentum to justify this premium, and the company recorded a net loss in FY21.
key_strengths: Gross margin of 54.97% is high, reflecting genuine brand pricing power in the Indian footwear market
Operating cash flow has been positive in all five of the last five years, with FCF growing to INR 670 Cr in FY25
Strong promoter holding of 50.16% and institutional ownership (29.31% DII) indicate confidence in management
key_risks: Revenue growth of 4.1% CAGR over nine years is sub-inflationary in real terms — this is a low-growth consumer franchise priced like a high-growth one
Net loss in FY21 (-89 Cr) breaks the consecutive positive earnings record I require, and FY24 profit declined to 263 Cr from 323 Cr in FY23
Finance costs have risen at 27.4% CAGR (largely Ind AS 116 lease capitalization), lifting D/E to 0.90 — above my 0.50 threshold
red_flags: P/E of 50.70 — more than 3x my maximum of 15
P/B of 6.39 — more than 4x my ceiling of 1.5
Price of INR 757 is 189% above the Graham Number of ~INR 262
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Bata is a household name with a century-old presence in India, but popularity is not the same as value. Mr. Market is asking INR 757 for every rupee of book value times 6.39 — and doing so for a company that has grown revenues at 4.1% annually for nine years and lost money in FY21. The forward P/E of 38.55 still implies decades of growth priced in. I do not speculate on futures; I pay for proven earnings power, and the price here contains no margin of safety.

The structural shift in finance costs — from INR 15 Cr in FY18 to INR 141 Cr in FY25 — reflects lease liabilities on retail stores under Ind AS 116, which is economically real even if accounting-driven. This raises the effective D/E and reduces the true free cash flow available to equity holders. I would require a price near INR 260-310 (the Graham Number range) before this business offers the protection of principal I insist upon.
